processing.text: DCP dissolved in acetone was mixed with milled PBS, dried for 24 h in a fume hood and then at 80 C for 12 h in a vacuum oven. Separate 50 g formulations were single-screw extruded at 140 C into 3 mm strands and pelletized. Portions were compounded in Dynisco LMM at 100 rpm for 10 min at 140 C, then injection-molded into dog-bone specimens.
processing.notes: 120 C hot-pressed discs are a separate route. Preparation temperatures and drying are not tensile-test conditions.

temper_or_heat_treatment.notes: No separately reported post-molding heat treatment for the selected tensile specimens.

conditioning.notes: Post-molding tensile conditioning is not stated. DCP/PBS drying is precursor preparation.

composition_or_purity.text: Nominal PBS / 10 wt.% Indulin AT softwood kraft lignin (percentage of total polymer mass), source R10 reactive series; 0.25 wt.% DCP added to PBS.
composition_or_purity.notes: The source says 0.25 wt.% DCP added to PBS. Its exact denominator and final retained DCP are not resolved; no final mass fractions, crosslink density, graft fraction, molecular architecture or chemical purity are inferred. Section 2.1 gives BioPBS FZ91PM/FZ91PB without resolving a single grade. Keep grade_id null; the R labels are study formulations, not commercial grades.

reinforcement.notes: Nominal feed loading, not an analyzed final mass fraction.

porosity.notes: No porosity reported for the selected tensile specimens.

orientation.notes: No specimen/material orientation stated for the selected result.

records.source_scope: Study-qualified DCP-reactive PBS / 10 wt.% Indulin AT softwood kraft lignin formulation R10 (Ewurum and McDonald 2025); lignin percentage is relative to total polymer mass. The nominal DCP-containing formulation and source-reported reaction distinguish this R-series from the corresponding B-series simple blend. Table 1 reports a nonzero gel fraction of 4.7% for R10; this supports the source reaction distinction, not a certified final network or an extra selected property. Different lignin loadings distinguish the four candidates. Processing routes, specimens, translated labels and measured differences alone do not create additional identities. Composite denotes a lignin-filled polymer formulation, not a pure molecular species or a continuous-fiber laminate. The source says 0.25 wt.% DCP added to PBS. Its exact denominator and final retained DCP are not resolved; no final mass fractions, crosslink density, graft fraction, molecular architecture or chemical purity are inferred. Section 2.1 gives BioPBS FZ91PM/FZ91PB without resolving a single grade. Keep grade_id null; the R labels are study formulations, not commercial grades. Section 2.4 (PDF p.4) determines contextual gel fractions on hot-pressed DCP cross-linked PBS-lignin material, not the injection-molded tensile dog-bones. These results support formulation-level reaction context only and do not determine the tensile specimens’ gel fraction or final network.
